bull.b: High gross margins (~75.8%) combined with double-digit revenue growth indicate neffy has favorable unit economics. Durable product-level profitability potential means incremental volume can flow largely to the bottom line once fixed commercialization costs moderate, supporting path to sustained profitability.

bull.t: Expanding payer access and affordability programs
bull.b: Broadening commercial coverage plus a $199 point-of-sale cash option and automatic claim-conversion reduce long-term prescription friction. These structural access and affordability initiatives increase realized demand, improve refill conversion and support a larger, more predictable installed patient base over time.

bull.t: Regulatory and international approvals widen market
bull.b: Label expansion to younger pediatric patients and approvals in Canada and the EU materially enlarge addressable markets. Partnered launches (e.g., ALK) create scalable international revenue channels that diversify geographic risk and extend the franchise beyond U.S. commercialization alone.

bear.b: Sustained, large negative operating cash flow creates persistent funding needs. Even with current cash balances, ongoing burn raises refinancing or dilution risk and constrains the company’s flexibility to invest in long-term initiatives unless cash conversion accelerates toward break-even as projected.

A cost base dominated by elevated SG&A to support field expansion and DTC ads places profit timing at risk. If salesforce ROI, refill conversion and gross-to-net improvements lag, persistent high SG&A will delay durable profitability and extend reliance on external funding.

Significant prior-authorization coverage gaps and ~22–23% abandonment structurally reduce filled prescriptions versus written demand. These persistent access barriers and lost fills compress realized revenue and hamper refill maturation, slowing the company’s ability to convert prescriptions into durable, repeatable sales.
